section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection of the letter Yud to Eretz Yisrael, based on the Maggid's teaching about two levels of fear (external and internal) corresponding to higher and lower wisdom, and how this manifests in the land.
section.t: And the explanation of the connection of the aspect of Yud to Eretz Yisrael
(that specifically in Eretz Yisrael it is "Rabi" with a Yud),
will be understood with an introduction from the teaching of the Maggid78
on the verse79
"A land which the L-rd your G-d cares for; the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are always upon it,"
for in the Zohar80
it asks: it is written81
"The eye of the L-rd is toward those who fear Him" in the singular, and it is written82
"The eyes of the L-rd are toward the righteous" in the plural.
And according to its simple meaning, it can be said that the wise are called83
"the eyes of the congregation."
And it is written84
"Wisdom cries out in the street" — two wisdoms: supernal wisdom and lower wisdom85.
And there is an internal fear and an external fear. External fear is the fear that comes from greatness86,
meaning that one does not recognize His inner essence, but only sees His greatness, and because of this he fears
[similar to what is explained in Tanya87,
that even when one has never seen the king and does not know him at all, but only sees that many great ministers bow to a certain person,
awe and dread will fall upon him],
and internal fear is when one recognizes His inner essence and importance, and because of this he fears and is ashamed before Him.
And this fear is called the fear of shame86.
And these two aspects of fear correspond to supernal wisdom and lower wisdom.
For in lower wisdom,
which is the aspect of Malchus,
the fear there is from greatness,
and in supernal wisdom
(that is, the aspect of Chochmah)
the fear is from inner essence.
And in order to have the fear of shame, one must recognize and comprehend His G-dliness,
and this is impossible except through a tzimtzum (contraction) in which He, as it were, contracts Himself so that He can be comprehended,
and this tzimtzum comes through a person making himself small, for "as water reflects a face back to a face."
And this is what is said regarding Eretz Yisrael: "the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are upon it,"
"eyes" in the plural,
meaning that in Eretz Yisrael there are two eyes,
external fear and internal fear.
For although the land is the aspect of Malchus, lower wisdom,
nevertheless, due to the advantage of the returning light, there is also in it the revelation of the supernal fear.
Analogous to how in the air close to the land there is more heat than in the middle air,
because the sun that strikes the land returns from it an illumination upward up to a third of the space.
And this is "a land which the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are upon it,"
"land" is Eretz Yisrael,
and in it there are two eyes: supernal wisdom and lower wisdom.
"From the beginning of the year to the end of the year,"
"beginning" is supernal wisdom
[and "beginning" is written deficiently (without an Aleph),
because the supernal wisdom that is revealed in lower wisdom
(the land)
does not have the Aleph that indicates the Most High].
(This concludes the content of the teaching of the Maggid).
And based on this, it will be understood what they said: "Every Rav is from Bavel and every Rabbi is from Eretz Yisrael"
[that in Eretz Yisrael it is "Rabi" with the addition of a Yud, which indicates wisdom],
for although Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of Malchus, lower wisdom and fear,
nevertheless,
since in the lower fear there is also a revelation of the supernal fear,
therefore in Eretz Yisrael it is "Rabi" with a Yud.
And this is also that the Yud added to "Rabi"
(from Eretz Yisrael)
is the aspect of the innerness of wisdom as above,
because the aspect of the fear of shame that comes from recognizing the inner essence is the aspect of the innerness of supernal wisdom,
and therefore the Yud in "Rabi"
(from Eretz Yisrael)
is the aspect of the innerness of wisdom,
and even to the aspect that flows from Ein Sof,
as above from the Baal Shem Tov.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the concept of absolute self-nullification (bittul) in Malchus, which must be applied in the three lines of Torah, service, and charity, enabling one to become an empty vessel to receive divine powers and achieve victory in the war against the evil inclination, leading to the future redemption.
section.t: 8) And this is what is said by his holy honor, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, in the discourse regarding the Yud at the back of the Dalet,
that the letter Yud indicates self-nullification and self-diminishment, namely the Malchus of Atzilus, which has nothing of its own,
that the nullification of the aspect of Malchus is
[not only the nullification of self-diminishment,
but rather]
the aspect of nullification of having nothing of its own,
which is the ultimate nullification.
And as above, that specifically in Malchus,
the aspect of lower wisdom,
the most supreme aspect of nullification is revealed.
And he continues in the discourse,
that this nullification must be in all three lines: Torah, service, and charity,
that in the study of Torah, mere nullification is insufficient
(the negation of coarseness of spirit)
rather it must be "in the aspect of utter self-nullification,"
and likewise in the line of service
(prayer)
there must be the nullification of "I am poor and needy," which is the aspect of nullification of the aspect of Malchus,
and likewise in the line of charity
(fulfillment of the commandments)
he explains with the analogy of lifting a heavy burden
(which is an analogy for the matter of fulfilling the commandments,
as above),
that in order to lift an extremely heavy burden
(it is not enough to contract oneself a little,
but rather)
one must contract oneself greatly.
And through this nullification
(in all three lines mentioned above)
he becomes an empty vessel that can contain,
receiving all the revelations and powers given from above to perform his service in Torah study, fulfillment of commandments, and the service of prayer,
and even to the point that he makes the connection and falsehood of the world transform into the planks of the Mishkan,
transforming the foolishness of idolatry into the foolishness of holiness.
For all this is through the nullification of an empty vessel,
for then he is a vessel to receive the powers given from above so that he can overcome the war against the evil inclination,
as explained in the discourse88
that for the sake of overcoming the war, they expend the hidden treasures from generation to generation
(what he stored himself and also what his ancestors stored)
and they are delivered through the officers of the army,
for specifically the men of the army
(the men of the army)
bring about the actual victory,
"the hosts of the L-rd,"
in all three interpretations of this,
as explained in the discourse89.
And the title "hosts of the L-rd" for Israel began from the time of the Exodus from Egypt,
as it is written90
"On that very day,
all the hosts of the L-rd went out of the land of Egypt,"
and from this it is also understood regarding the future redemption,
that it will be similar to the redemption from Egypt, as it is written91
"As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
that through this there will be the revelation of the future redemption, when there will be wonders even relative to the matters that were in the Exodus from Egypt92,
and afterwards there will be "Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust"93
and He is among them.
